common_definitions.compact_domain: K(delta,T,R)={s in C:1+delta<=Re(s)<=R, |Im(s)|<=T}, for every delta>0, finite T>=0, and finite R>=1+delta
common_definitions.schedules: S_k in {k!,2(k!)} for every integer k>=1; diagonal m_k=2^k
common_definitions.summand: a_(j,N)(s)=-q_N(g_j) Log_0(1-exp(-s ell(g_j)/q_N(g_j)))=q_N(g_j) sum_(r>=1) exp(-r s ell(g_j)/q_N(g_j))/r; g_j is the jth certified content-one owner, so q_N(g_j)=1
common_definitions.branch: Log_0 is the analytic branch defined by the displayed absolutely convergent series for |exp(-s ell/q)|<1 and normalized to 0 as Re(s)->infinity
common_definitions.pointwise_majorant: M_(j,N,K)=-q_N(g_j) log(1-exp(-(1+delta)ell(g_j)/q_N(g_j))); for content one this is M_(j,K)=-log(1-exp(-(1+delta)ell(g_j)))

rows.indices_and_coupling: fix schedule choice and k; N=S_k; let m->infinity through the certified owner order
rows.majorant_obligation: prove sum_(j>=1) M_(j,S_k,K)<infinity for the exact certified owners
rows.specific_interchange: identify lim_m sum_(j<=m) a_(j,S_k) with the infinite owner sum uniformly on K
rows.prerequisites: factor derivation; certified cofinal content-one enumeration; exact lengths; branch binding

rows.indices_and_coupling: fix m; N=S_k; let k->infinity separately for S_k=k! and S_k=2(k!)
rows.majorant_obligation: for each j<=m prove sup_k sup_(s in K)|a_(j,S_k)(s)|<=M_(j,K)<infinity; finite sum_(j<=m) M_(j,K)
rows.prerequisites: factor derivation and branch binding; content-one q=1 must be proved applicable, not inferred from an executed result

rows.indices_and_coupling: for each schedule first m->infinity at fixed k, then k->infinity
rows.majorant_obligation: prove one k-independent summable sequence M_j(K) with |a_(j,S_k)(s)|<=M_j(K) for every j,k,s in K
rows.specific_interchange: lim_k sum_(j>=1)a_(j,S_k)=sum_(j>=1)lim_k a_(j,S_k), uniformly on K
rows.prerequisites: AN-1 for every k; component limits; certified cofinal enumeration; uniform dominated tail

rows.indices_and_coupling: for each schedule first k->infinity at fixed m, then m->infinity; compare with AN-3
rows.limit_order: lim_(m->infinity)[lim_(k->infinity)L(m,S_k;s)] and equality with the AN-3 order
rows.majorant_obligation: prove the same k-independent summable M_j(K) and convergence of each a_(j,S_k) on K
rows.specific_interchange: justify lim_m lim_k L=lim_k lim_m L and identify both with sum_j lim_k a_(j,S_k)
rows.prerequisites: AN-2 for every m; AN-3 dominated tail; common certified owner order

rows.indices_and_coupling: m=m_k=2^k and N=S_k, separately for S_k=k! and S_k=2(k!)
rows.majorant_obligation: prove a k-independent summable M_j(K), component convergence, and sup_(s in K) sum_(j>2^k)|a_(j,S_k)(s)|<=sum_(j>2^k)M_j(K)->0
rows.specific_interchange: identify the coupled diagonal limit with the common AN-3/AN-4 iterated limit
rows.prerequisites: certified cofinal diagonal; both schedule branches; AN-3/AN-4 common limit; uniform tail

finite_diagnostic_boundary: The prospective k<=8 prefix and m in {8,16,32,64,128} panels remain unexecuted serialization diagnostics. They have no convergence, cofinality, majorant, interchange, or scientific-result force.
non_global_boundary: No tail theorem, infinite scalar specialization, factor theorem, owner enumeration, limit identity, recovery statement, obstruction, or Route credit is asserted.
